## a test filter
🎯 Test Filter: Mem-Mirror*,Lat-L3-*
  Running tests matching pattern
  Default: cycles=1 for quick targeted runs
  CLI overrides supported (e.g. duration=60 cycles=5)

## the quick test
🚀 TMR Quick Test Mode: plan=quick, the stability tests once
  Quick test uses reduced memory (60% reserve) for faster validation
  CLI overrides supported

## every parameter note
  Minimum Page Size: regular
  Maximum Page Size: large
  hugechunk: 2GiB
  blkround: down
  Topology Detection: windowsv2
  CPU Pinning: Skipping first 1 CPU(s)
  CPU Pinning: Disabled
## the header of a release build
Startup Mode & Parameters:
  Command Line: tmr.exe memory=50% cputype=cores cpus=100% skip-cores=0 cycles=1
  Build Type: ✅ Release (optimized)
## the header of a debug build
Startup Mode & Parameters:
  Command Line: tmr.exe
  Build Type: ❌ Debug (unoptimized)
## the parameters, given and defaults
  RUST_LOG: info (logs to .\logs\TMR_YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS.log)
  Explicit Parameters: memory=50%, --startup-debug
  Default Parameters: cputype=threads (default), errors=log (default)
## the parameters, a backtrace set and none given
  RUST_LOG: debug (logs to .\logs\TMR_YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS.log)
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1
## cores
  CPU Type: cores (avoiding SMT/Hyperthreading)
## threads
  CPU Type: threads
## a core range left out
  CPU Filter: excluding core id range 0-7 (Stage 1)
## a share of the CPUs
  CPU Count: 50% of 6 available = 3 thread(s)
## pinned, a CPU skipped, SMT doubling avoided, both limits
  Error Mode: Log and continue
  Using 3/6 cores for testing
  CPU Assignment: [2, 4, 6]
  Skipping first 1 CPU(s) for system responsiveness
  Avoiding SMT doubling (using physical cores only)
  Test Suite Timing: 3 cycles or 600s max (whichever first)
  SIMD Support: SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, AVX, AVX2

## unpinned, halting, cycles only
  Error Mode: Halt on first error
  Using 3/6 cores for testing
  CPU Assignment: [2, 4, 6] ⚠️ NUMA placement only, pinning is off
  Test Suite Timing: 1 cycles (no time limit)
  SIMD Support: SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, AVX, AVX2

## panicking, time only
  Error Mode: Panic on error (debug mode)
  Using 3/6 cores for testing
  CPU Assignment: [2, 4, 6]
  Test Suite Timing: 60s duration (unlimited cycles)
  SIMD Support: SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, AVX, AVX2

## no limits
  Error Mode: Log and continue
  Using 3/6 cores for testing
  CPU Assignment: [2, 4, 6]
  Test Suite Timing: Unlimited cycles and duration
  SIMD Support: SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, AVX, AVX2

## large pages are checked
Checking Large Page access
## what the check did
🔍 Large Page Diagnostic
  Privilege: assigned and enabled
  Test allocation: 2 MiB, succeeded
## large pages usable
🎉 Large Pages: ✅ ENABLED and tested successfully!
   TMR will use 2MB large pages for optimal performance

## large pages not usable, and minpage needs them
⚠️  Large Pages: Not available, and minpage=large needs them, so the run will stop
   before allocating. Set them up (tmr.exe --setup-large-pages, elevated), or rerun
   with minpage=regular to test on standard 4KB pages: every test still runs, but
   slower memory traffic is less stress, so marginal errors that only appear at
   full bandwidth may go undetected

## large pages not usable, and minpage doesn't need them
⚠️  Large Pages: Not available - TMR will use standard 4KB pages
   Performance impact: ~5-10% slower memory allocation
   Every test still runs and every pattern is still checked, but slower
   memory traffic is less stress, so marginal errors that only appear at
   full bandwidth may go undetected

## realtime on every CPU
⚠️  priority=realtime with a worker on every logical CPU: the console and input can freeze until the run ends. Leave a core free (skip-cores=1) or use priority=high.
